title: An 8-foot Bigfoot was spotted in Connecticut last month. It’s far from New England’s first.
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Kevin Klimas reported an 8-foot Bigfoot sighting in Voluntown, Connecticut, verified by the Bigfoot Field Researchers Organization.
Since 1994, there have been 126 verified Bigfoot sightings in New England, tracked by the Bigfoot Field Researchers Organization.
Boston University professor Eva Garrett states there's no scientific evidence of Bigfoot, despite reported sightings and fossil links to Gigantopithecus.

title: I will miss my friend Margo, who told me to grieve, but not too much
author: Meredith Goldstein
bullets: Margo Howard, daughter of Ann Landers, and former advice columnist, passed away at 86 last month.
Howard began writing 'Dear Prudence' for Slate in her late 50s and later penned 'Dear Margo' for The Boston Globe.
She offered practical and empathetic advice, emphasizing the importance of moving beyond past grievances and seeking happiness.

title: Red Sox bats, Payton Tolle’s 14 strikeouts stifle Athletics, 13-1
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: Payton Tolle struck out 14 batters as the Red Sox defeated the Athletics 13-1 at Fenway Park.
The Red Sox extended their winning streak to nine games, improving their record to 64-51 on the season.
Boston's offense recorded 15 hits and multiple high-scoring innings, including a five-run second inning.

title: A.J. Brown and Christian Gonzalez continue sharpening each other’s games at Patriots training camp
author: Colin McCarthy
bullets: A.J. Brown and Christian Gonzalez competitively face off in Patriots training camp, enhancing their skills for the upcoming season.
Gonzalez, seeking a new contract, uses trash talk to prepare Brown for top receivers, while maintaining professionalism.
Brown aims to bounce back with over 1,000 receiving yards last year, bolstered by Drake Maye's deep-ball proficiency.

title: New Red Sox catcher Adley Rutschman to begin rehab assignment this weekend
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: Red Sox acquisition Adley Rutschman will start a rehab assignment Saturday with the Triple-A Worcester Red Sox.
Rutschman was placed on the injured list on July 20 due to left wrist inflammation.
Acquired from the Orioles, Rutschman has 19 home runs and a .764 OPS this season.

title: 5 must-watch movies & TV shows streaming right now
author: Kevin Slane
bullets: 'Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender', a continuation of the original series, is now streaming on Paramount+.
'You, Me & Tuscany', starring Halle Bailey and Regé-Jean Page, is available on Peacock.
'Ted Lasso' Season 4, featuring Jason Sudeikis, streams on Apple TV with a new women's team storyline.

title: Could Garrett Crochet return to Red Sox in a bullpen role?
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: Garrett Crochet may return to the Boston Red Sox as a reliever due to ongoing recovery from injuries.
Interim manager Chad Tracy indicated Crochet is unlikely to return as a starting pitcher this season.
Crochet has started throwing again after setbacks and is open to contributing in any role this year.

title: Lost a python? Boston Animal Care and Control might have it.
author: Heather Alterisio
bullets: A ball python, temporarily named 'Tippy,' was found near Ellington Street in Dorchester on Thursday.
Boston Animal Care and Control took custody of the python, left in a cage near community garden beds.
Officials ask for information on the python's owner via 617-635-1800 or [email protected].

title: Tommy DeVito bests Drake Maye, and other takeaways from Patriots’ training camp scrimmage
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Tommy DeVito led Team Blue to a 22-15 victory over Team White in the Patriots' scrimmage.
DeMario Douglas impressed for Team Blue, securing six catches and two touchdowns, including a 50-yard play.
Injury concerns persist for cornerback Carlton Davis, who is expected to miss more training sessions.

title: A closer look at Harwich, voted the best town on Cape Cod by Boston.com readers
author: Kristi Palma
bullets: Harwich was voted the best town on Cape Cod by over 850 Boston.com readers in an informal poll.
Harwich offers nearly 11 miles of tidal shoreline along Nantucket Sound and Pleasant Bay, featuring more than 20 beaches.
The town boasts cultural, historical, and recreational attractions, appealing to varied interests across age groups.
